parts.text: Define specific latent heat of fusion.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A student sets up the apparatus shown in Fig. 3.1 in order to investigate the melting of ice.

{{figure:figure_3_1.png}}

The heater is switched on.
When the pure ice is melting at a constant rate, the data shown in Fig. 3.2 are collected.

| voltmeter reading / V | ammeter reading / A | initial mass of beaker plus water / g | final mass of beaker plus water / g | time of collection / minutes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12.8 | 4.60 | 121.5 | 185.0 | 5.00 |

Fig. 3.2

The specific latent heat of fusion of ice is $332\text{ J g}^{-1}$.
parts.text: State what is observed by the student that shows that the ice is melting at a constant rate.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the data in Fig. 3.2 to determine the rate at which

1. thermal energy is transferred to the melting ice,

2. thermal energy is gained from the surroundings.
